name: Lamotrigine
route_note: Oral tablets, chewable dispersible tablets, orally disintegrating and extended-release tablets; slow titration required.

discovery.note: Developed from a hypothesis linking antifolate activity to anticonvulsant effects; lamotrigine turned out to be only a weak antifolate. Year is the first patent filing by the Wellcome Foundation, which disclosed the synthesis.

tagline: Broad-spectrum anticonvulsant and bipolar depression preventive with a rash warning
summary: Lamotrigine is a broad-spectrum anticonvulsant also used to prevent mood episodes, particularly depression, in bipolar I disorder. It is well tolerated and has a comparatively favourable pregnancy profile, but must be titrated slowly to reduce the risk of serious rash.
mechanism: Lamotrigine inhibits voltage-gated sodium channels in a use-dependent way, stabilising neuronal membranes and reducing presynaptic release of glutamate. It also has effects on high-voltage-activated calcium channels.
Its mood-stabilising mechanism is not fully understood but is thought to relate to reduced glutamatergic excitability.
uses: Focal and generalised tonic-clonic seizures (monotherapy and adjunct)
Maintenance treatment of bipolar I disorder

history.title: First launch
history.detail: Lamictal is launched in the UK.

history.title: US approval
history.detail: The FDA approves lamotrigine for adjunctive treatment of partial seizures.

history.title: Bipolar disorder
history.detail: The FDA approves lamotrigine for maintenance of bipolar I disorder.

history.title: SANAD
history.detail: The UK SANAD trial (Marson et al., Lancet 2007) finds lamotrigine the preferred first-line drug for focal epilepsy.

history.title: Generics
history.detail: Generic lamotrigine becomes available in the US.

history.title: Cardiac warning
history.detail: The FDA adds a warning about arrhythmia risk in patients with structural or ischaemic heart disease based on in vitro class IB antiarrhythmic activity.

pk.half_life: about 25–33 hours (about 13 h with enzyme inducers, about 70 h with valproate)

safety.boxed_warning: Serious skin rashes, including Stevens-Johnson syndrome and toxic epidermal necrolysis; risk increases with high starting doses, rapid titration and co-administration with valproate.

facts: Oestrogen-containing contraceptives and pregnancy markedly increase lamotrigine clearance, often requiring dose adjustment.
Lamotrigine is used to prevent bipolar depression but has limited efficacy against acute mania.
